answer: The strongest cheap check I know is Signed home energy audit with installer attestation. It demands an audit and retrofit logged in one name, and the haven is that the proof is bound to one body, one device, one history. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that an audit and retrofit logged in one name — so privacy survives, and the forge is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. One clone is cheap; a hundred are a small business with no revenue. The kernel is the point where the farm's spreadsheet turns red.
